candidate.answerReason: External circle tangency gives AB=8. Similar tangent-radius triangles give AC/BC=5/3, and C lies beyond B, so AC=BC+8. Solving gives BC=12.

methods.label: Similar tangent-radius triangles
methods.explanation:
The circles touch externally, so their center distance is
\[
AB=5+3=8.
\]
A common external tangent has both centers on the same side of it, so it cannot cross the segment \(AB\). Since its intersection \(C\) lies on ray \(AB\), the point \(C\) is beyond \(B\). Therefore \(AC=BC+8\), with \(BC>0\).

Let \(P\) and \(Q\) be the points where the line touches the circles centered at \(A\) and \(B\), respectively. A radius to a tangency point is perpendicular to the tangent, so \(AP\perp CP\) and \(BQ\perp CQ\). The right triangles \(CAP\) and \(CBQ\) have the same acute angle between the center line and the tangent, so they are similar. Their corresponding radii and hypotenuses give
\[
\frac{AC}{BC}=\frac{AP}{BQ}=\frac{5}{3}.
\]
Substituting \(AC=BC+8\) and multiplying by the positive denominators gives
\[
3(BC+8)=5BC.
\]
Thus \(24=2BC\), so \(\boxed{BC=12}\), choice D.
